newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga mulls mid-Norway condensate pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Saga mulls mid-Norway condensate pipeline.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Thursday it would begin evaluating the possibility of laying a pipeline to land condensate from the Haltenbank area in the Norwegian Sea off mid-Norway.
Saga has made two gas and condensate discoveries, dubbed as Kristin and Lavrans, in the area.

"The company wishes, with the other licensees, to look at the possibilities of a joint pipeline to mid-Norway for light oil (condensate) from the Kristin and Lavrans discoveries, and from the Aasgard and Tyrihans fields," Saga said in a statement.

Norway's largest listed oil company said no decision had been taken on the location for landing a pipeline. But, it said, the possibility of a joint pipeline from the Haltenbank fields should be evaluated and clarified this year.
If implemented, the pipeline would be the first to shore light oil from this part of the Norwegian continental shelf.
"Accordingly, we will also look at the synergies of a coordinated development of the fields, as Saga believes that this would give the highest value added for the fields," the statement said.
A joint solution would also increase the competitiveness of Haltenbanken gas, it said.
Saga has not yet tested the Kristin dicovery, but plans to start some time in April and conclude testing before the seasonal ban on drilling in the area on environmental grounds comes into force.
The company added that Norway should keep the allocation of new gas sales contracts to a minimum in 1997.
"Next year there wil be a better understanding of which fields it would be most rational to develop, based on considerations of socio-economic and resource utilisation," it said.
"Consequently, a postponement of major allocations to 1998 would be the most sensible thing to do, based on Saga's evaluation."
